name: SikaSeal-300 Glass and Weather Seal
paste:
SIKASEAL®-300 GLASS AND WEATHER SEAL: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaSeal®-300 Glass and Weather Seal, April 2023, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/a/sikaseal_-300_glassandweatherseal.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaSeal®-300 Glass and Weather Seal where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description. SikaSeal® 300 is a neutral-curing silicone sealant with a high movement capability and excellent adhesion to a wide range of substrates.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Aluminium
    - Composite materials
    - Panels(ACP)
    - Glass
    - Metals
    - Coated and painted metals
    - Plastics
    - Wood
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.4.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaSeal®-300 Glass and Weather Seal
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: A NEUTRAL-CURING SILICONE SEALANT WITH A HIGH MOVEMENT CAPABILITY AND EXCELLENT ADHESION TO A WIDE RANGE OF SUBSTRATES
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 01.02) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Excellent adhesion
    - High movement capability
    - Weather resistant
    - Outstanding UV resistance
    - High strength
    - Interior & Exterior
    - Permanent flexibility
2.4 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: 1-C silicone
    - Colour: Transparent
    - Density: ~1.03 kg/l
2.5 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shore A hardness: ~25
    - Tensile strength: ~1.0 N/mm²
    - Modulus of elasticity in tension: ~0.4 N/mm²
    - Tensile strain at break: ~900%
    - Movement capability: ± 50%
    - Tear propagation resistance: ~4 N/mm
    - Skinning time: ~40 minutes
    - Tack free time: ~180 minutes
2.6 Service temperature. -40°C to +150°C approx. STANDARD THERMAL RESISTANCE ~180°C SHORT TERM THERMAL RESISTANCE
    | ~200°C | For 4 hours. |
    | ~220°C | For 1 hour. |
2.7 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 300ml Cartridge, 25 cartridges per box
    - Shelf life: 12 months (when stored below 25°C)
    - Storage conditions: Below 25°C

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation. Surfaces must be clean, dry and free from oil, grease and dust, loose and friable materials. Advice on specific applications and surface pretreatment methods is available from the Technical Service Department.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application method / tools.
    - Application: After suitable joint and substrate preparation, SikaSeal®-300 Glass and Weather Seal is gunned into place. Joints must be properly dimensioned as changes are no longer possible after construction. For optimum performance the joint width should be designed according to the movement capability of the sealant based on the actual expected movement. The minimum joint depth is 6 mm and a width / depth ratio of 2:1 must be respected. For backfilling it is recommended to use closed cell, sealant compatible foam backer rods e.g. high resilience polyethylene foam rod. If joints are too shallow for backing material to be employed, we recommend using a polyethylene tape. This acts as a release film (bond breaker), allowing the joint to move and the silicone to stretch freely. For more information please contact our Technical Department.
    - Tooling and finishing: Tooling and finishing must be carried out within the skin time of the adhesive. When tooling freshly applied SikaSeal®-300 Glass and Weather Seal press the adhesive to the joint flanks to get a good wetting of the bonding surface.
4.3 Cleaning of equipment. Uncured SikaSeal®-300 Glass and Weather Seal may be removed from tools and equipment with Sika® Remover-208 or another suitable solvent. Once cured, the material can only be removed mechanically. Hands and exposed skin should be washed immediately using Sika®Handclean Towel or a suitable industrial hand cleaner and water do not use solvents.
4.4 Limitations and important considerations. Restrictions on Use: Most Sikasil® WS, FS, SG, IG, WT, AS and other engineering silicone sealants manufactured by Sika are compatible with each other.Sikasil® WS and FS sealants are compatible with SikaGlaze IG sealants. All other sealants have to be approved by Sika before using them in combination with SikaSeal®- 300 Glass and Weather Seal. Where two or more different reactive sealants are used, allow the first to cure completely before applying the next. Do not use SikaSeal®-300 Glass and Weather Seal on pre-stressed polyacrylate and polycarbonate elements as it may cause environmental stress cracking (crazing). The compatibility of gaskets, backer rods and other accessory materials with SikaSeal®-300 Glass and Weather Seal must be tested in advance. Joints deeper than 15 mm should be avoided. The above information is offered for general guidance only. Advice on specific applications will be given on request.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5°C to +40°C
5.3 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.4 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaSeal®-300 Glass and Weather Seal, April 2023, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/a/sikaseal_-300_glassandweatherseal.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SikaSeal®-300 Glass and Weather Seal, version 12/09/2022, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/x/SikaSeal%20300%20Glas%20&%20Weather%20Seal.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
